Judge In Brady Case Allows Him To Use Medical Marijuana
And Asks Prosecutor To Consider Dropping The Marijuana Charges

Pete Brady Update

April 9, 1999

Special To MarijuanaNews:

See
Life As A Drug War Prisoner by Pete Brady

Pete Brady, the High Times, Hemp Times and Cannabis Culture journalist facing prison for his journalistic activities and for possession of medical marijuana, is continuing his battle for freedom in rural Butte County, California.

Brady has been acting as his own attorney, an experience he describes as "highly educational for everyone involved."

"I think that the judge and district attorney, and even some of the police, are seeing that the war on plants is counterproductive and a waste of tax dollars," Brady said. "In some of the motions I filed, I included as exhibits my articles from High Times and other magazines, showing the human cost of this war."

Although Judge Barbara Roberts ruled against Brady’s "demurrer" motion which argued that California’s medical marijuana law should have prevented his arrest, she urged Deputy District Attorney Mark Noel to examine Brady’s medical pot recommendation and to consider dropping the marijuana charges. Roberts had previously handed down an important ruling that allowed Brady to use his medicine while on bail or probation.

April 9, 1999

Special To MarijuanaNews:

See
Life As A Drug War Prisoner by Pete Brady

Pete Brady, the High Times, Hemp Times and Cannabis Culture journalist facing prison for his journalistic activities and for possession of medical marijuana, is continuing his battle for freedom in rural Butte County, California.

Brady has been acting as his own attorney, an experience he describes as "highly educational for everyone involved."

"I think that the judge and district attorney, and even some of the police, are seeing that the war on plants is counterproductive and a waste of tax dollars," Brady said. "In some of the motions I filed, I included as exhibits my articles from High Times and other magazines, showing the human cost of this war."

Although Judge Barbara Roberts ruled against Brady’s "demurrer" motion which argued that California’s medical marijuana law should have prevented his arrest, she urged Deputy District Attorney Mark Noel to examine Brady’s medical pot recommendation and to consider dropping the marijuana charges. Roberts had previously handed down an important ruling that allowed Brady to use his medicine while on bail or probation.

This would still leave Brady facing a felony charge for illegal cacti, as well as a probation violation.

"I strive for hope, but the reality is that these charges are harming my health and clouding my future," Brady admits. "The drug laws are very strict and have been harshly interpreted and implemented for a long time. There is a lot of case law and institutional intertia that lends foundation to imprisoning non-violent drug defendants."

With a major hearing scheduled for April 19, Brady feels that it is unwise for him to try to continue representing himself.

He said that grow guru Ed Rosenthal, along with the head of California NORML Dale Gieringer, had offered to help him with attorney’s fees.

"I’m finding that the marijuana movement is like a family," he said. "We’re waking up to the fact that we are a persecuted class of people, victims of discrimination and ignorance. We are learning to present our cause as a struggle for human rights and dignity. And we are learning to work together. That means a lot to me."
